claims.statement: NIS2 requires covered entities to address supply-chain security and consider vulnerabilities and cybersecurity practices of direct suppliers and service providers.

contrary_evidence: NIS2 does not mandate a standardized supplier passport, and buyers may insist on their own questionnaire or recognized certifications.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: buyer-questionnaire mappings and acceptance outcomes turn one assessment into more reusable procurement access
fingerprint.customer: small EU field-service and O&M vendors supplying essential or important entities
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: large contractors, cyber assessors, and insurance brokers require or refer the credential down their supply chain
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: evidence vault, control mapping, assessor attestation, remediation queue, expiration tracking, and buyer export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the vendor pays when its evidence passport is assessed and whenever a buyer-specific package is exported
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a tender, onboarding, or renewal questionnaire asks for verifiable supplier cybersecurity practices

founder_fit: Good automation and family renewable-channel fit; qualified partners handle security attestations while the founder builds mappings and workflow.
risks: A passport could create false assurance if evidence is stale.
National implementations and buyer standards diverge.

structure.control_point: the accepted supplier-security evidence package attached to a covered buyer's tender or vendor renewal
structure.critical_dependency: buyer acceptance of the credential, qualified assessment partners, and accurate mapping to national NIS2 implementation

thesis: Create a reusable, evidence-backed cyber passport for small renewable O&M, building-control, and field-service vendors selling to NIS2-covered entities. The paid trigger is a tender or annual vendor renewal blocked on security evidence, not generic cybersecurity awareness. All commercial numbers, including capital_required_pln, are unvalidated hypotheses.
title: NIS2 Supplier Evidence Passport for Field-Service Vendors
uncertainties: Vendor willingness to pay versus buyer-funded assessment is unvalidated.
The minimum credential buyers accept is unknown.
